Assertion records

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

GeneBench-Pro: Evaluating Multistage Statistical Reasoning in Genomics, Quantitative Biology, and Translational Biomedicine · paper method: The reported primary metric uses Python binary grading: every prespecified target field must satisfy its exact-match rule or absolute numeric tolerance for the run to pass, and the free-text reasoning field is collected for qualitative analysis but is not graded.

Permanent record ID: assertion.genebench.pro.binary-grading.20261112

Request a correction

Continue to private email

Copy the email draft

Start a public GitHub correction · GitHub requires sign-in.

  • Binary scoring gives no primary-metric partial credit, so a late failure after correct intermediate steps scores the same as an immediate failure.

Continue to private email

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Native speakers manually translate the prompt template, 79 attribute values and 36 scenarios into ten languages. Twenty-three models generate stories; a three-LLM ensemble extracts profiles covering nineteen demographic attributes.
  • The human harmfulness panel has 247 UK participants working in English and is 89.9% White. Participants rate 50 associations each, rather than validating every generated story.
  • The extraction audit covers 30 English/French stories. Extraction errors and nonuniform abstention can affect associations; the checked sample does not establish reliability in every language.
  • Pairwise co-occurrence does not decompose attribute mediation and is not interpreted causally; the human panel is one culturally bounded normative reference.
  • Main section 3 and Figure 10 ask harmful-stereotype agreement from strongly disagree to strongly agree; Appendix F.2 instead describes acceptability from not acceptable to fully acceptable. This wording/direction conflict remains unresolved.
  • Section 3 describes median rating aggregation, while section 4.3 and Figure 4 explicitly compare per-association mean human and mean model ratings over 1,580 associations. These are distinct stated summary scopes.

Request a correction

Continue to private email

Copy the email draft

Start a public GitHub correction · GitHub requires sign-in.

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Eleven US native-English adult participants produce 200 conversations with eight anonymized original models. Diagnostic data are self-reported; conversations are not independent participants.
  • GPT-4o-mini suggests question subsets that participants may revise. Golden responses are participant-edited after viewing original and preference-informed model outputs, rather than independent wholly human-written references.
  • Eleven evaluation models predict participant annotations. Default does not use future turns; Omniscient includes privileged profiles. Mistral Large draft scores and Kendall tau are supplementary and excluded from the Composite.
  • Pooled tests assume conversation independence despite repeated participants. Conversation-level Pearson r=-0.097 and model-level Spearman rho=-0.36 have different statistical units and are not interchangeable.
  • The human baseline has three raters and seven conversations. Small imbalanced culturally restricted samples and self-report limit interpretation; the authors explicitly exclude clinical validation and safety-critical deployment use.

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.

Judge selection/calibration uses 1,687 majority-vote labels from 120 trajectories of three solvers and three human raters; 97.1% agreement is that sample result, not an independently held-out accuracy guarantee.
  • Eight runs are planned per task. Mean Criteria@3 uses three runs selected lexicographically by task ID; Pass@8 is any complete success and Pass^8 requires all eight. Model-caused failures are zero; infrastructure failures are excluded, leaving 156-160 tasks per paired comparison.
  • Difficulty selection retains hard worlds under three frontier filtering models, and clarification/human-in-the-loop tasks are excluded.
  • The authors report a self-preference stress test with the judge also solving the benchmark and interpret its 37.1% middle/lower score as no material self-preference. That limited author test does not independently rule out judge bias.
  • This repair uses the v2 paper count only. A prior reference to a separate 100-task leaderboard/card conflict is not reasserted: those distinct artifacts were not read or reconciled here. No private corpus, score reproduction, independent bias audit or source-contribution inference is claimed.
